title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is an English typescript numbered 76. It is not Grothendieck's manuscript. It is filed (archive page 123) among the 1965 notes on motivic Galois theory, between two handwritten French pages about polarisations and involutions on motivic groups G_C = D_C(M). Mathematically it is one step in a classical, Chevalley/Zariski-style proof that the image of a complete variety under a rational map to projective space is closed.

Setting:
- V is a complete variety with a morphism φ: V → P^T, given locally on an open cover U^{(i)} by regular functions φ_0^{(i)},...,φ_T^{(i)}.
- Q is a point of the closure of the image, with homogeneous coordinates x_0,...,x_T and x_k(Q) ≠ 0.

Argument:
1. Using the inclusion k(x_0/x_k,...,x_T/x_k) ≅ k(φ_0/φ_k,...,φ_T/φ_k) ⊂ k(V), take a place, i.e. a homomorphism into (k,∞), of the coordinate field of the image with centre Q.
2. Extend it to a place of k(V) (Chevalley's extension theorem for places). By completeness of V (valuative-criterion form), this place has a centre Q' on V.
3. Choose k_1 with φ_{k_1}(Q') ≠ 0. Then F = φ_k/φ_{k_1} is regular at Q'.
4. If φ_k(Q') were 0, then F(Q') = 0, so the place sends φ_{k_1}/φ_k to ∞. But that value equals (x_{k_1}/x_k)(Q), which is finite. Hence φ_k(Q') ≠ 0.
5. So the φ_j/φ_k are regular at Q' and take the values (x_j/x_k)(Q). That is, φ(Q') = Q, so the image is closed.

This is a standard textbook argument, likely from a translated Russian lecture course (the '(k,∞)' notation for places and 'point of the field' for place suggest a Shafarevich-school text). Unsure.
errors: The equality (φ_{k1}/φ_k)(Q') = (φ_{k1}/φ_k)(Q) mixes 'value at a point' with 'value of the place'. Strictly, what holds is that the place takes the value x_{k1}/x_k(Q) on φ_{k1}/φ_k. Regularity of F at the centre Q' then gives the contradiction. The notation is sloppy but the argument is correct.
'the point of the field k(V)' means a place of k(V) (Chevalley terminology). This is not an error, just older terminology.

ideas.what: Image of a complete variety under a morphism to projective space is closed, proved via extension of places and existence of centres
ideas.modern_name: Properness / valuative criterion; images of proper maps are closed
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chevalley, Zariski, Weil (classical); EGA II §7 for the valuative criterion
ideas.where_published: EGA II §7 (valuative criteria); EGA II 5.4 (proper morphisms)

ideas.what: Extension of a place from a subfield to the function field

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled page of a standard English-language textbook or lecture typescript (not Grothendieck's) proving closedness of images of complete varieties via places. It is entirely routine and unrelated to the surrounding motivic Galois notes.
transcription_corrections: The sentence ending 'regular function in Q′' has no full stop in the image, and the parenthetical begins on the next line.
The page is an English typescript with handwritten displayed formulas. It is not in Grothendieck's hand, unlike the neighbouring French manuscript pages.
